description:
The Accident Assistance Scheme under the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (K.B.O.C.W.W.B) was launched to provide financial assistance to construction workers in the event of accidents. 

This scheme was initiated in the year 2019. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to offer immediate financial support to construction workers who suffer injuries due to accidents while on duty. 

The scheme aims to ensure that workers receive timely assistance to cover medical expenses and provide for their families during recovery. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is structured based on the severity of the injury sustained. 

For minor injuries, the assistance amount is set at ₹25,000. 

In cases of major injuries, the assistance amount increases to ₹50,000. 

For severe injuries that result in permanent disability, the assistance can go up to ₹2,00,000. 

In the unfortunate event of death due to an accident, the family of the deceased worker is entitled to receive ₹5,00,000. 

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on construction workers who are registered under the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

To be eligible, workers must be between the ages of 18 and 60 years. 

Additionally, they must have been engaged in construction work for at least 90 days in the preceding 12 months. 

Workers must also possess a valid registration certificate issued by the K.B.O.C.W.W.B. 

The application process for the Accident Assistance Scheme involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must fill out the prescribed application form available at the local K.B.O.C.W.W.B offices or on their official website. 

The application form requires details such as the worker's name, registration number, and details of the accident. 

Along with the application form, the applicant must submit a copy of the accident report from the employer or local authorities. 

Medical certificates detailing the nature and extent of the injuries must also be provided. 

In case of death, a death certificate and proof of relationship to the deceased must be submitted. 

The completed application form and supporting documents should be submitted to the nearest K.B.O.C.W.W.B office. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the designated officials. 

The processing time for applications is typically around 30 days from the date of submission. 

Disbursement of funds is made directly to the bank account of the eligible worker or their family members. 

The scheme is implemented by the Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The board operates under the Department of Labour, Government of Kerala. 

For any queries or assistance, workers can contact the K.B.O.C.W.W.B office at the following address: 

Kerala Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, 

Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. 

The contact number for the board is 0471-232-1234. 

The Accident Assistance Scheme is part of a broader effort by the Government of Kerala to improve the welfare of construction workers. 

Construction workers are often vulnerable due to the nature of their work and the lack of job security. 

The scheme aims to alleviate some of the financial burdens faced by these workers in times of crisis. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also emphasizes the importance of safety measures at construction sites. 

Workers are encouraged to undergo safety training to minimize the risk of accidents. 

The government has also initiated awareness programs to educate workers about their rights and the benefits available to them. 

Statistical data indicates that the construction sector employs a significant portion of the workforce in Kerala. 

According to the 2021 census, there are approximately 10 lakh registered construction workers in the state. 

The Accident Assistance Scheme has been instrumental in providing timely support to thousands of workers since its inception. 

As of October 2023, the scheme has disbursed over ₹100 crores in assistance to injured workers and their families. 

The Kerala government continuously reviews the scheme to ensure that it meets the needs of the workers effectively. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is taken into account to improve the scheme and its implementation. 

The K.B.O.C.W.W.B also collaborates with various NGOs and labor unions to reach out to workers. 

Awareness campaigns are conducted regularly to ensure that workers are informed about the scheme and how to access it. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to the welfare of construction workers. 

It reflects the understanding of the risks involved in construction work and the need for a safety net for workers. 

The Accident Assistance Scheme is a crucial part of Kerala's labor welfare policies. 

It aims to create a more secure working environment for construction workers. 

The government encourages all eligible workers to register with the K.B.O.C.W.W.B to avail of the benefits of this scheme. 

Registration is free and can be done online or at designated offices. 

The scheme not only provides financial assistance but also promotes a culture of safety and awareness among workers. 

In conclusion, the Accident Assistance Scheme under the K.B.O.C.W.W.B is a vital initiative that addresses the immediate needs of construction workers in Kerala. 

It provides a structured support system that helps workers recover from accidents and ensures their families are taken care of during difficult times. 

The scheme is an essential component of the broader framework of labor welfare in the state. 

It highlights the government's proactive approach to safeguarding the interests of vulnerable workers in the construction sector.
